newsitem.title: FINLAND: HSBC MIDLAND SEES FINNISH RATE CUT IN SHORT TERM.
newsitem.headline: HSBC MIDLAND SEES FINNISH RATE CUT IN SHORT TERM.

text.p: HSBC Midland Bank said in a Nordic Outlook research note received on Thursday that Finland was more likely to cut key interest rates below German levels than raise them.
HSBC also said Finland was on track for membership of Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
"We believe it is more likely in the short term that Finnish rates are cut (below German levels) rather than raised, on the back of a strong markka," HSBC said.
The Bank of Finland's key tender rate has been at 3.00 percent -- on par with the German repo rate -- since October.
"In Finland, inflationary worries still remain very remote," HSBC said.
It forecast a pick-up in Finnish CPI to 1.5 percent this year from a projected 0.6 percent in 1996.
"Finland will be eligible for EMU ... We think there is a good case for Finland to be priced as a core country -- narrowing towards 10-20 bp for the 10-year bund spread," HSBC said.
At 1250/1050 GMT, Finnish 10-year bond yields traded 25 basis points over corresponding German Bunds.
Finnish EMU entry was not, however, guaranteed, HSBC said.
"The Maastricht criteria should be met even on a reasonably strict interpretation," it said, adding: "The only significant sticking point is Finland's debt/GDP ratio."
HSBC forecast Finland's EMU debt at 61.0 percent in 1997 -- one percentage point over the EMU entry limit, but noted that the debt/GDP trend was heading downwards.
"Politically, the willingness to join is strong, too, underlined by the entry of the markka to ERM ... in the face of Swedish reluctance to take the plunge," HSBC said.
It expected DEM/FIM to trade in a stable 2.95-3.04 range.
The markka's ERM central parity to the German mark is 3.04.
HSBC forecast that Finnish economic growth would outpace
other Nordic countries and the European Union, but due to
subdued inflation no rate hike was expected this year.
"Finland is set to enjoy a period of both high growth and
low inflation with no rate hike in sight for 1997," it said.
"The Finnish economy should ... see its fourth consecutive
year of below average (EU) inflation and above average GDP
growth in 1997," HSBC said.
"We expect Finland to top the Nordic growth league with a
4.2 percent GDP increase," it said, referring to this year. Its
1998 Finnish GDP growth forecast was 3.5 percent.
Key figures in HSBC Midland's forecast on Finland:
Consumer spending +2.6 +3.5 +3.3
Investment +2.5 +5.4 +7.4
Unemployment 16.4 15.5 15.0
HSBC Midland's Nordic Outlook was dated January 1997.
